title: Two session-load runs at once share one sandbox clone, so the later one records only a git checkout error
goal: Two session-load runs started at once each get their own sandbox clone and record their own rows, so neither records a CalledProcessError from git checkout (seen 2026-10-27: a run beside two others recorded one row and run errors 1 with git checkout -q -- . exit 128, where a rerun alone gave 99 rows)

run: import subprocess,sys; c=[sys.executable,"-c","import sys; sys.path.insert(0,\"_tools\"); import bench_core; print(bench_core.scratch_dir())"]; a,b=(subprocess.run(c,capture_output=True,text=True).stdout for _ in (1,2)); sys.exit(0 if a!=b else 1)

gates.question: How does a session-load run keep its sandbox clone apart from a run started at once, and what happens to its clones when it ends?
options: scratch_dir() is a per-process run-<pid>-<hex> directory under scratch_base(), and Bench.close() removes the run's clones and bare origins
scratch_dir() is a per-process run directory, and Bench.close() keeps the clones
only session-load names its clones per run, scratch_dir() stays shared
gates.recommendation: scratch_dir() is a per-process run-<pid>-<hex> directory under scratch_base(), and Bench.close() removes the run's clones and bare origins
gates.reason: runs share nothing, and the 1.3 GB clones do not pile up; raw logs stay
gates.answer: scratch_dir() is a per-process run-<pid>-<hex> directory under scratch_base(), and Bench.close() removes the run's clones and bare origins
